result.title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding
result.summary: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TriRouter，一种电极空间路由框架，用判别保持、掩码鲁棒与 latent 补偿三条路径，并按可见通道可用性校准路由权重，以提升 EEG 运动想象在通道缺失下的解码准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属 BCI 信号解码应用，其「latent」指电极特征补偿而非推理状态，路由也只依据通道可见性，未涉及视觉证据使用、推理状态生成或停止决策，缺乏可供核查的实质线索。
